extracted.intended_audience: Incident Management Teams, Incident Commanders, Public Information Officers, operations leaders and incident dispatchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Incident Management Team members—particularly Public Information Officers, operations leaders, and incident dispatchers—on internal/external communications, Unified Command procedures, media/community relations, resource/accountability practices, and demobilization during multi-jurisdictional incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations leaders and incident dispatchers need to maintain radio discipline on the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates untimely use of congested airwaves and maintains a professional sounding incident for all listeners (e.g., agency administrators, the media).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to cellular/portable communications during disasters
rubrics_metrics.description: In areas of high cellular coverage, cellular companies may provide portable cells and portable phones to responders under FCC licensing clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with logistics to assure they know how to access this service (often provided without cost, including call costs) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional external communications expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: External communications (briefing agency administrators, working with dispatch, tracking vendors, transmitting cost information, etc.) must be of the highest professional level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team members should be aware that external communications reflect on the team; maintain professionalism in tone and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Status Summary (ICS Form 209) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Incident Status Summary (ICS Form 209) is the most off-incident reviewed document during deployment; completeness, accuracy and timeliness are paramount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are deadlines for ICS Form 209 that must be met because the document is used to allocate resources. It must be on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and confirm required off-incident document transmission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Many documents (e.g., ICS Form 209s, cost estimates) are required to be transmitted off an incident throughout its life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assure you know them all; reconfirm early with the receiver a timetable and method to be used for each to avoid wasted time tracking down late or incomplete documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency administrator briefings best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency administrator briefing times and methods are normally set during the Transition Briefing; IC or deputy will routinely do them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review latest intelligence just prior to briefing to transmit best information; be forthright and honest—administrators want the best 'feel' for the incident to make off-incident decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize importance of external communications to all team members
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness of the importance of external communication by all team members helps the team be perceived as structured and accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting deadlines and professional presentation under difficult tasks improves perception; reminders/tips (e.g., local Internet providers may provide free access) can assist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify legitimacy of Unified Command participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the incident legitimately requires Unified Command—'allow all agencies with responsibility for the incident, either geographical or functional, to manage an incident.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear, ask your agency administrator; be cautious of agencies being included or pacified without jurisdiction or functional responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a single ordering point in Unified Command
rubrics_metrics.description: Has a single ordering point been established? Incident Commanders must agree on the method for ordering additional resources/supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs must immediately agree what single point will be used, advise their agency, and ensure incident personnel from their agency know and abide by this decision to avoid adverse impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine cost-share status immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this a cost share incident? Some agencies do cost sharing as policy; others may not understand it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer impasse to agency administrator immediately; expect financial responsibility to be associated with incident responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order cost-share technicians when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If cost sharing will occur, order cost share technicians to produce necessary agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance/administration personnel on the team may lack time or expertise; have a technician represent each agency involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and verify agency-responsibility maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Have maps accurately delineating each agency’s area of responsibility on-hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not intimately familiar with areas, have agency administrator or designee verify map accuracy; this is important for cost-share and operational clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Unified Command objectives meeting all agencies' needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish Unified Command objectives that meet all involved agencies' needs; use blank Incident Objectives, ICS Form 202 to aid development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep development as objectives (not tactical actions). Objectives should be negotiated and mutually acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish management staff and negotiate lead/deputy roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish management staff to fill lead section chief and officer roles; negotiate deputy roles when agencies insert staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider keeping Incident Management Team intact as leads while negotiating limited deputy roles; ensure agency administrator reviews any negotiated staffing settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information release single-source agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: All agencies on the incident must agree to a single source for development of information released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information section may include personnel from all agencies but released stories must be identical to avoid problems in Unified Command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual agreement on incident facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement on incident facilities—their location, purpose and size—must be mutual among agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and announce agreements from IC meetings so all team members understand decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team attitude and intra-team behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Team attitude will set the tone for the incident; team intra-actions must continue as normal and react equally to all ICs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer conflicts of direction to the team IC; aim for counterparts to feel accepted as full members after the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open, honest, and cooperative with counterparts
rubrics_metrics.description: Openness and honesty are required so the agreed command structure will work effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting team attitude or cooperation become a source of problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to train counterparts
rubrics_metrics.description: Incident Management Team members should expect to be relied upon to pass along experience and possibly train counterparts in their functional roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can become a full-time task and may develop future members of your team—approach it positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain approachable and open to input
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members must demonstrate untiring desire for input and interaction to stimulate cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set an example of cooperation to encourage common-cause work among agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collocate management functions and Incident Command Post (ICP)
rubrics_metrics.description: With minor exceptions, all management functions must be collocated, including the ICP—multiple ICPs are not true Unified Command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure physical co-location to avoid fragmented command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish agency-specific finance/administration personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate agency-specific finance/administration personnel (may be deputies) to ensure proper procedures and documentation are followed for each agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These personnel report to the finance/administration section chief but assure each agency's processes are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish agency-specific time recorders
rubrics_metrics.description: Have agency-specific time recorders within the incident's finance/administration section to meet specific time recording requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They report to the finance/administration section chief and handle agency-specific tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish agency-specific compensation/claims personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign agency-specific compensation/claims personnel to handle claims according to the jurisdiction-specific process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These people work for and report to the finance/administration section chief to avoid settlement delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-share negotiation confidentiality and division-by-division split
rubrics_metrics.description: When cost sharing, a division-by-division percentage split is required for each operational period; ICs assign percentages privately with cost share technicians only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much pressure is implied if someone from an IC's agency is present/observing; negotiate privately to reduce pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations chiefs must verify resource use each operational period
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations section chiefs must verify where each resource was actually used during each operational period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This verification requirement (including air operation branch directors for air resources) should be made known early so tracking methods can be employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting large incidents into zones requires single objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Splitting a geographically large incident into zones can work but there can only be one set of incident objectives; negotiate objectives between zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area Command is preferable to coordinate efforts and prioritize resources when multiple zones are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred multi-team arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: If two teams are assigned, options include one team primary with the other as deputies (second-best) or establishing Area Command; rotating teams by operational period is not recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotating teams causes loss of command continuity and risk of details falling through the cracks; best solution is releasing one team at direction of agency administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for resource scarcity and avoid embellishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect scarce resources and long delays; plan creatively and flexibly; do not embellish reports to increase priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nontraditional approaches (rental dozers, local crews) and be honest—embellishments seldom work and can backfire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organized news conferences for media requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When media request interviews with the IC, consider organized news conferences to meet deadlines and media needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertise time, find adequate space, use good visual aids, brief presenters on likely questions, set a timeframe, have PIO open and facilitate the session, and be ready to 'rescue' IC(s) if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Messaging and logistics for large numbers of destroyed structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Information section theme should emphasize saved vs. destroyed counts; organize triage to count foundations and identify destroyed structures quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use addresses/assessor plot maps for identification; offer escorted visits for owners with proof of residency, provide marked agency transportation and compassionate staff, consult mental health services, consider ALS availability, and manage media presence for privacy and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damage assessment ordering and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Order specialized resources for damage assessment when numbers are known; consider county assessor/building departments for expertise and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know what you want from damage assessment—counts, photos, prevention information—and plan for staffing/time to assemble qualified assessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evacuation coordination roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Evacuations are a law enforcement function, but operations/liaisons trigger the need and must coordinate closely with law enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get the highest-ranking law enforcement official, install them as a branch director for law enforcement, involve county emergency services coordinator for shelters/transports, place PIOs in shelters, and negotiate reoccupation procedures with law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage pressure to reoccupy residences cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist internal and external pressure to reoccupy too quickly; do not inhibit operations or force premature reentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance human desire to return with operational safety and potential need to re-evacuate; involve occupants when appropriate and plan reentry deliberatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community relations and briefings for citizens and elected officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize public briefings for affected communities; coordinate with local elected officials and present layperson-friendly information with visual displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily single-page informational handouts and inclusion of elected officials in briefings/planning meetings improve relations; prepare final packages of incident products for officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: VIP visit procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate a function responsible for VIPs, brief them on incident history/projections/issues, and provide facility tours and front-line visits when practical and safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use marked PPE and vehicles, plan overflights with licensed aircraft, offer follow-up briefings and contact information to limit return visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability through guidelines and performance ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Team guidelines should outline expectations and performance ratings should incorporate those expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make forms available, staff a central collection location, distribute forms off-incident per policy, and use honest ratings as learning tools for the team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing substandard or non-performance
rubrics_metrics.description: If performance detrimentally impacts the incident, release the individual and send them home with immediate supervisor notification and written documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer personnel problems to the IC immediately; determine if transgressions warrant punitive action and request a specialized investigator when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base/camp rules of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams should have base/camp rules of conduct available in portable word processing, detailing acceptable/unacceptable conduct and attire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post rules on bulletin boards, include in IAPs as appropriate, and enforce them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and manage mutual aid resource utilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Require periodic review by operations on the effectiveness and value of mutual aid resources; avoid holding them longer than needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider using Type II/III engines where appropriate, request state-owned engines when suitable for cost, and plan early for demobilizing mutual aid (vehicle inspections take time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization planning using an operations matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations should produce a matrix listing resource types for each operational period for a minimum of three days to project future needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the matrix often; modify numbers as operational periods complete assignments, and use it to begin demobilization planning—plan early, review often, demobilize unneeded resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for new incident types and capability gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect new types of incidents (large Hazmat, civil disturbances, earthquakes, floods, tsunamis) requiring skills beyond typical wildland fire experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain knowledgeable technical specialists where team corporate knowledge is lacking; develop interpersonal skills to coordinate with diverse agencies; be prepared for fiscal constraints, pressure to perform, personal/family concerns, and political issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to operate within or support Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams may be requested to function within EOCs at various government levels and may need to assist in delegations of authority and roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear delegation of roles and authorities is required; teams may need to assist in developing them and must ensure delegation covers legal/authority boundaries for actions expected.
